Source: IATA (2024b) 2.2.2 SAF Market Factors The availability of biomass-based SAF is a function of the availability of biomass to produce SAF, which competes with use for bioenergy and other projects. Forecasts for SAF produced from biomass and electrons are provided in Section 2.1.4. Various domestic and international policies have been key drivers in determining the production of SAF relative to other fuels, as well as impacting where the fuel is used geographically. The most notable global policy is the European Union’s ReFuelEU SAF requirement of 2% in 2025, growing to 6% by 2030 and 70% by 2050 (European Union Aviation Safety Agency 2025).6 The U.K. SAF mandate is 2% in 2025, growing to 10% in 2030 and 22% by 2040 (U.K. Department for Transport 2024). The United Kingdom limits HEFA contribution in forward years to enable advanced pathways. There are also numerous aviation goals and targets that include accelerated deployment of SAF production. The Renewable Fuel Standard is a primary market driver for domestic biofuels, and there are categories with requirements set by the EPA annually. The Renewable Fuel Standard assigns obligated parties (e.g., fuel refiners and importers) a renewable volume obligation each company is required to blend based on a percentage of the company’s total fuel sales. The Renewable Fuel Standard allows for fuel flexibility to meet the requirements—for example, SAF, biodiesel, and renewable diesel all meet the advanced biofuel category meaning similar compliance values though different production costs. EPA manages and tracks the Renewable Fuel Standard through Renewable Identification Numbers, where various biofuels are assigned values based on energy density relative to ethanol. Renewable Identification Number values can impact biofuel economics. HEFA plants generally produce both fuels, and producers may make production volume decisions based on Renewable Identification Number values, which may lead producers to favor renewable diesel over SAF in production. The 2022 Inflation Reduction Act created the 45Z credit to encourage domestic biofuels production. The 2025 credit available to American-controlled biofuels producers was $1.75/gal for SAF and $1.00/gal for other biofuels meeting various criteria. The 45Z credit was amended in the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act, providing clarification on allowable feedstocks from the United States, Canada, and Mexico, and the credit is $1.00/gal for all biofuels meeting criteria for biofuels produced between Jan. 1, 2026, and Dec. 31, 2029.
